MARS FRONTIER NAVIGATOR

Complete Project Architecture & Backend Technical Documentation

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

==================================================

  1. PROJECT OVERVIEW
    ==================================================

Project Name: Mars Frontier Navigator

Project Description:

Mars Frontier Navigator is an intelligent navigation platform designed to help astronauts explore the Martian surface safely and efficiently.

The system analyzes geographical data, terrain elevation, slope angles, radiation levels, and potential hazards to calculate the safest and shortest walking routes between two locations on Mars.

The platform also estimates astronaut resource consumption, including oxygen, battery power, and estimated walking time.

Main Objectives:

  • Calculate the safest and shortest walking routes on Mars.
  • Avoid dangerous slopes and hazardous geographical areas.
  • Analyze radiation levels and terrain conditions.
  • Estimate oxygen consumption and battery usage.
  • Provide estimated mission duration.
  • Display geographical information through an interactive map.
  • Provide geographical layers and scientific points of interest.

Database Technology:

  • PostgreSQL: Main relational database.
  • PostGIS: Spatial data storage and geographical queries.
  • PostGIS Raster: Raster-based geographical data support.
  • GIST Indexes: Accelerate spatial queries.

SQL Files:

  1. 01_extensions.sql

Purpose:
Enable the required PostgreSQL extensions.

Required extensions:

  • PostGIS
  • PostGIS Raster
  1. 02_tables_schema.sql

Purpose:
Create the main database tables.

Main data structures:

TERRAIN_GRID:

  • Geographical coordinates.
  • Elevation values.
  • Slope angles.

HAZARD_ZONES:

  • Radiation zones.
  • Rock hazard polygons.
  • Geographical hazard information.

Other logical entities:

  • TILES
  • WAYPOINTS
  • MISSIONS

Purpose:
Create GIST spatial indexes to improve the performance of geographical queries.

  1. 04_seed_nasa_data.sql

Purpose:
Insert sample geographical data.

Required reference areas and datasets:

  • Mount Sharp.
  • MOLA data.

Database Responsibilities:

  • Store geographical and terrain information.
  • Store radiation and hazard zones.
  • Support spatial queries.
  • Retrieve geographical information efficiently.
  • Provide data required by the pathfinding engine.

The backend consists of four main layers:

  1. Database Layer
  2. Algorithms and Engine Layer
  3. Models Layer
  4. API Layer

A. DATABASE LAYER

Location:
app/database/

FILE: connection.py

Responsibilities:

  • Establish PostgreSQL connections.
  • Manage database connection pooling.
  • Handle database connection configuration.
  • Provide database access to backend services.

FILE: spatial_queries.py

Responsibilities:

  • Retrieve terrain information using PostGIS.
  • Retrieve geographical elevation data.
  • Detect obstacles and hazardous areas.
  • Calculate geographical distances.
  • Retrieve spatial information required by the pathfinding engine.

B. ALGORITHMS AND ENGINE LAYER

Location:
app/engine/

FILE: grid_builder.py

Purpose:
Convert geographical data retrieved from PostgreSQL/PostGIS into a 2D Grid that can be processed by the pathfinding algorithm.

Responsibilities:

  • Retrieve geographical coordinates.
  • Retrieve elevation and slope information.
  • Convert geographical data into grid cells.
  • Prepare the grid for pathfinding.

FILE: cost_function.py

Purpose:
Calculate the movement cost of each grid cell.

The cost function considers:

  • Distance.
  • Slope angle.
  • Radiation level.

Required cost formula:

Total_Cell_Cost = Distance + (Slope_Angle × 2.5) + (Radiation_mSv × 5.0)

Important Rule:

Any slope greater than 25 degrees must be considered completely dangerous.

Its cost must be set to Infinity so the pathfinding algorithm excludes that cell.

FILE: astar_pathfinder.py

Purpose:
Implement the A* pathfinding algorithm to calculate the safest and shortest route.

Responsibilities:

  • Find an optimal path between starting and ending points.
  • Avoid dangerous slopes.
  • Avoid geographical obstacles.
  • Avoid areas with high radiation.
  • Use the cost function to evaluate possible paths.
  • Return the selected route.

FILE: telemetry_calc.py

Purpose:
Calculate astronaut resource consumption based on the selected route.

Required calculations:

  • Oxygen consumption.
  • Battery consumption.
  • Estimated walking time.

Calculations must consider:

  • Total route distance.
  • Terrain conditions.
  • Slope and route difficulty.

C. MODELS LAYER

Location:
app/models/

FILE: request_models.py

Purpose:
Define the structure of incoming JSON requests.

Required information:

  • Starting point coordinates.
  • Ending point coordinates.
  • Mission type.

FILE: response_models.py

Purpose:
Define the structure of outgoing JSON responses.

Required information:

  • Route coordinates.
  • Elevation information.
  • Total distance.
  • Estimated walking time.
  • Oxygen consumption.
  • Battery consumption.
  • Safety index.
  • Warnings.

D. API LAYER

Location:
app/api/v1/

FILE: router.py

Purpose:
Register and combine all API endpoints.

FILE: path_endpoints.py

Purpose:
Handle path calculation requests.

Main endpoint:

POST /api/v1/pathfinding/calculate

Responsibilities:

  • Receive starting and ending coordinates.
  • Validate the request.
  • Retrieve geographical information.
  • Call the pathfinding engine.
  • Calculate resource consumption.
  • Return the final route and telemetry data.

FILE: layers_endpoints.py

Purpose:
Handle geographical map layer requests.

Responsibilities:

  • Retrieve radiation layers.
  • Retrieve slope layers.
  • Retrieve thermal layers.
  • Retrieve elevation layers.
  • Return geographical features to the frontend.

Base URL:
http://localhost:8000

API Version:
v1

ENDPOINT 1: CALCULATE ROUTE

Method:
POST

Endpoint:
/api/v1/pathfinding/calculate

Description:

Calculate the safest and shortest walking route between two geographical points on Mars, estimate resource consumption, and calculate a safety index.

REQUEST BODY:

{
"start_point": {
"lat": -4.58,
"lon": 137.42
},
"end_point": {
"lat": -4.62,
"lon": 137.50
},
"mission_type": "geology"
}

REQUEST PARAMETERS:

start_point:

  • Type: Object
  • Description: Starting geographical coordinates.

start_point.lat:

  • Type: Float
  • Description: Starting latitude.

start_point.lon:

  • Type: Float
  • Description: Starting longitude.

end_point:

  • Type: Object
  • Description: Destination geographical coordinates.

end_point.lat:

  • Type: Float
  • Description: Destination latitude.

end_point.lon:

  • Type: Float
  • Description: Destination longitude.

mission_type:

  • Type: String
  • Description: Mission category, such as geology.

EXPECTED RESPONSE:

{
"status": "success",
"path": [
{
"lat": -4.58,
"lon": 137.42,
"elevation": -2100
},
{
"lat": -4.59,
"lon": 137.44,
"elevation": -2050
}
],
"telemetry": {
"total_distance_meters": 4850,
"estimated_time_mins": 75,
"oxygen_consumed_percent": 12.5,
"battery_consumed_percent": 8.0,
"safety_index": "94%"
},
"warnings": []
}

RESPONSE FIELDS:

status:

  • Type: String
  • Description: Request execution status.

path:

  • Type: Array
  • Description: Calculated route coordinates.

path.lat:

  • Type: Float
  • Description: Latitude of each route point.

path.lon:

  • Type: Float
  • Description: Longitude of each route point.

path.elevation:

  • Type: Number
  • Description: Elevation of each route point.

telemetry:

  • Type: Object
  • Description: Resource consumption information.

total_distance_meters:

  • Type: Number
  • Description: Total route distance in meters.

estimated_time_mins:

  • Type: Number
  • Description: Estimated walking time in minutes.

oxygen_consumed_percent:

  • Type: Number
  • Description: Estimated oxygen consumption percentage.

battery_consumed_percent:

  • Type: Number
  • Description: Estimated battery consumption percentage.

safety_index:

  • Type: String
  • Description: Calculated route safety index.

warnings:

  • Type: Array
  • Description: Route warnings and potential hazards.

ENDPOINT 2: GET GEOGRAPHICAL LAYERS

GET

/api/v1/layers/{layer_type}

Description:

Retrieve geographical layers to display on the interactive map.

SUPPORTED LAYER TYPES:

  • thermal

PATH PARAMETERS:

OPTIONAL QUERY PARAMETERS:

]

ENDPOINT 3: GET POINTS OF INTEREST (POIs)

Method:
GET

Endpoint:
/api/v1/poi

Description:

Retrieve scientific points of interest on Mars, such as Boxwork formations and the Curiosity rover's location.

OPTIONAL QUERY PARAMETERS:

  • Type: String

EXAMPLE REQUEST:

GET /api/v1/poi?region=mount_sharp

EXPECTED RESPONSE:

{
"pois": [
{
"id": "poi_01",
"title": "Boxwork Formations",
"lat": -4.59,
"lon": 137.46,
"description": "Unique mineral ridges studied by Curiosity.",
"rover_image_url": "/assets/rover_photos/boxwork_01.jpg"
}
]
}

RESPONSE FIELDS:

  • Type: Array
  • Description: List of scientific points of interest.

id:

  • Type: String
  • Description: Unique POI identifier.

title:

  • Type: String
  • Description: POI name.

lat:

  • Type: Float
  • Description: Latitude.

lon:

PHASE 1: DATABASE AND GIS LAYER

Objective:
Establish the geographical database infrastructure.

Tasks:

  1. Install and configure PostgreSQL.
  2. Enable PostGIS and PostGIS Raster extensions.
  3. Create the required database tables.
  4. Create the terrain_grid table to store geographical coordinates, elevation, and slope angles.
  5. Create the hazard_zones table to store radiation and rock hazard polygons.
  6. Create the required spatial indexes using GIST.
  7. Insert sample NASA geographical data for Mount Sharp and MOLA.

Expected Result:

A working PostgreSQL database capable of storing and retrieving geographical information.

PHASE 2: ALGORITHMS AND ENGINE

Objective:
Develop the core pathfinding and resource calculation algorithms.

Tasks:

  1. Implement grid_builder.py.
    • Retrieve geographical data from PostGIS.
    • Convert geographical coordinates into a 2D grid.
    • Calculate movement costs.
    • Consider distance, slope, and radiation.
    • Exclude slopes greater than 25 degrees using Infinity.
    • Implement the A* algorithm.
    • Find the safest and shortest route.
    • Avoid obstacles and dangerous areas.
    • Calculate oxygen consumption.
    • Calculate battery consumption.
    • Estimate walking time.

Expected Result:

A working algorithm engine capable of calculating safe routes and estimating astronaut resource consumption.

PHASE 3: CORE APIs AND SWAGGER

Objective:
Expose backend functionality through RESTful APIs.

Tasks:

  1. Initialize FastAPI.
  2. Configure Uvicorn.
  3. Configure CORS in main.py.
  4. Configure automatic Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.
  5. Implement the pathfinding endpoint.
  6. Implement geographical layers endpoints.
  7. Implement the POI endpoint.
  8. Implement the health check endpoint.
  9. Connect the API layer with the database and algorithms engine.

Expected Result:

A working API that allows the frontend to communicate with the backend.

PHASE 4: TESTING AND VALIDATION

Objective:
Verify the correctness of the algorithms and resource calculations.

Tasks:

  1. Create test_astar.py.
    • Verify that the algorithm avoids dangerous slopes.
    • Verify that the algorithm avoids obstacles.
    • Verify that the algorithm avoids dangerous geographical areas.
    • Verify oxygen calculations.
    • Verify battery calculations.
    • Verify estimated walking time.

Expected Result:

A tested backend with validated pathfinding and telemetry functionality.

FILE: requirements.txt

fastapi
uvicorn
psycopg2-binary
shapely
numpy

  1. Slopes greater than 25 degrees must be excluded from route calculations by assigning Infinity as their cost.
  2. The pathfinding algorithm must consider distance, slope angle, and radiation level.
  3. The A* algorithm must avoid geographical obstacles and high-radiation areas.
  4. All geographical queries must use PostgreSQL/PostGIS.
  5. Spatial indexes must use GIST to improve geographical query performance.
  6. The backend must expose RESTful APIs through FastAPI.
  7. Swagger documentation must be accessible through /docs.
  8. CORS must be configured to allow frontend communication.
  9. Request and response structures must be validated using Pydantic models.
  10. The telemetry engine must calculate oxygen consumption, battery consumption, and estimated walking time.
  11. The API must return route coordinates, elevation information, telemetry, safety index, and warnings.
  12. The backend must provide geographical layers and scientific points of interest to the frontend.

The following implementation details must be finalized before development:

  1. DATABASE SCHEMA

Define exact columns, primary keys, foreign keys, spatial data types, and relationships for all database tables.

  1. SAFETY INDEX

Define the mathematical formula used to calculate the route safety percentage.

  1. TELEMETRY CALCULATIONS

Define the exact oxygen and battery consumption formulas.

  1. COST FUNCTION

Confirm the units and normalization of distance, slope, and radiation values to ensure the cost formula is mathematically consistent.

  1. API RESPONSE STRUCTURE

Confirm that frontend and backend developers use the same JSON structures.

  1. POINTS OF INTEREST

Define the database structure and data source for scientific locations and rover images.

  1. FRONTEND INTEGRATION

Confirm the map coordinate reference system and geographical data format.
